segments.title: 第36章 新書上架
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 36: New Book Launch

Xu Youyu was born into a family with a rich literary background.

Her father was a professor in the literature department at Qianjiang University, and her grandfather had also been a teacher in the history department.

Her mother graduated from the history department of Qianjiang University and was one of her grandfather's students, while her maternal grandfather had also been a schoolteacher in a small town in his early years.

So, from a very young age, Xu Youyu had the means and environment to be exposed to all kinds of literary works, steeped in her family's literary atmosphere for a long time.

But around the fifth or sixth grade, this little sapling brimming with literary spirit seemed to start growing crooked after being secretly lent a romance novel by a friend.

However, perhaps because of the different upbringing she received, Xu Youyu didn't get too engrossed in romance novels.

She always felt that the female leads in them were immersed in love and romance all day long, lacking their own opinions, which became quite boring after reading a few.

Later, she read novels from the male-oriented category, and from then on, she walked a path of no return.

In Xu Youyu's view, the book "I'm Really Not a Star" was a standard, gratifying, and straightforward web novel about the entertainment industry.

If she were to actually critique it, she could seriously analyze its various strengths and weaknesses.

But if the author, Li Luo, were the one asking, Xu Youyu could only offer a couple of chuckles and say, "It's just so-so, barely readable."

Li Luo: "..."

If it's barely readable, why are you still reading it?

Just last night, you were calling me 'master' over and over, yet today it has become 'so-so'?

"If you haven't read it, my advice is to not read this kind of novel," Xu Youyu said with a couple of coughs. "You can get addicted if you read too much. Studying is what's important for us."

There was nothing wrong with what she said.

But coming from Xu Youyu's mouth, it somehow felt a little hypocritical.

The corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched. He managed a nod, not having the heart to expose her true colors, and then continued to eat with his head down.

...

August 22nd, Friday.

Wenyue Group, Changning City, Urban Fiction Editorial Team.

Today was the day for new books to be launched for paid reading.

Editor Qianzhou was checking the list for any errors or omissions. Afterward, he could submit it to the backend technical operations team to grant these new books permission to upload VIP chapters.

In this batch of new books, there were two that Qianzhou was quite optimistic about.

One was Reigniting's "I'm Really Not a Star." Its concurrent readership had already risen to 2,000 before its launch. As long as it was written well and the plot remained stable, it might have a chance to become the first book under him to break the 3,000 average subscription mark, earning it 'Prestige' status.

The other was Sleeping Early Will Make You Taller's "The Literary Era." Its current concurrent readership had reached 1,000. Although its performance was not as good as the former, Qianzhou knew it was a slow-burn novel, and having such a start was already quite good.

In contrast, the new books from the editor next to him, Qingyue, were much more miserable this week.

The one with the best performance, "Max-Level Guide to Korean Entertainment"—it was unclear if the author's mentality collapsed because they failed to secure a Sanjiang recommendation spot, or if it was simply a lack of ability—but in any case, the subsequent plot had fallen apart.

The concurrent readership had plateaued all the way, and was now only around 800, even lower than "The Literary Era."

Although he was embarrassed to admit it, Qianzhou felt a tiny bit of satisfaction in his heart.

After all, Qingyue had only joined Wenyue Group about half a year ago. Qianzhou himself had only been on the job for just over a month. Both of them were still considered newcomers in the team.

Moreover, although the chief editor or editor-in-chief never said it outright, most categories basically had a configuration of one chief editor and three executive editors.

So, with two senior executive editors already in the team, recruiting two new editors within half a year made the intention of fostering competition quite obvious.

No one wanted to be eliminated.

Therefore, as soon as Qianzhou joined, Qingyue had indirectly revealed the fact that she was a female editor in contracted author groups and some new Qidian author groups.

Then, leveraging the success brought by Korean entertainment novels over the past few months, she advertised herself as having produced one author with ten-thousand subscriptions and five with 'Prestige' status within half a year.

But in reality, all six of these books were Korean entertainment novels.

And that ten-thousand-subscription book was actually written by a veteran author using a new pen name. Feeling too embarrassed to approach their old editor, they picked a new one, letting her get lucky.

But this didn't stop the "Qingyue" editor brand from gradually becoming more attractive to authors.

This led to Qianzhou having a very difficult start.

After all, they were both new editors, but she had been there a few months longer than him, had solid results to back her up, and was a beautiful and kind female editor.

In terms of author resources, Qianzhou really couldn't compete at all.

But precisely because of this, being able to firmly beat Qingyue in the performance of new books being launched this week still made Qianzhou feel a faint sense of joy.

However, just as Qianzhou was feeling pleased, the chief editor, Hongdou, coughed twice and clapped his hands to get the team's attention.

Then he said, "I have an announcement for you all."

"The Urban Fiction category will be launching a new writing contest, mainly focusing on the entertainment industry."

"You should all be aware that Korean entertainment novels have always been the dominant force in this area, with incredible momentum."

"But recently, a Korean entertainment novel was reported to the higher-ups. We've been verbally instructed to pay attention to the impact and to guide authors to promote our own country's culture."

"So the editor-in-chief has arranged for a writing contest to respond to the call, advocating for the promotion of national cultural characteristics and local entertainment symbols and forms."

"Works participating in the contest will be given some extra traffic. Consider it a way of answering to the higher-ups."

"Each of you, give me a list later. Don't try to get by with old books. Try to find new ones that fit the contest's requirements."

"In the future, if any authors want to write new entertainment novels, recommend they try this direction as well."

"Boss," Qianzhou couldn't help but ask after hearing Hongdou's words, "do the new books that are about to be launched today count?"

"They count." Hongdou nodded and glanced at the time. "The deadline is noon today. As long as it's a new book that hasn't been launched yet, it's within the scope of the contest."

"Okay, boss!" With a face full of joy, Qianzhou opened Word and got right to it, first writing down "I'm Really Not a Star" and "The Literary Era."

But just then, Chief Editor Hongdou paused for a moment, then added softly, "For the time being, sign fewer Korean entertainment novels. All Korean entertainment novels that are to be signed must be reported to me for review."

"Also, those of you with Korean entertainment novels under your charge, remind the authors to do more research when they write. If they don't understand the historical facts, they shouldn't just write nonsense. They should stick to writing face-slapping power fantasies."

"That's all for this matter. If you have any other questions, come find me privately."

...

Exactly twelve noon.

Li Luo and Xu Youyu, each sitting at their desks in their bedrooms, uploaded the first VIP-access, paid chapter for their new books.

Shortly after, they both received a message from their editor, Qianzhou.

Qianzhou: The Urban Fiction category has a new writing contest for entertainment novels.

Qianzhou: I've signed you both up for it. There might be some extra recommendations in the future.

Qianzhou: Also, I took a look. If your results are good and you get selected for an award later, the first prize is ten thousand yuan. You guys can pay attention to that too.

Seeing the editor's message.

Xu Youyu raised an eyebrow. She wasn't that interested in the ten thousand yuan, but she did want the extra recommendation spot resources.

As for Li Luo, his eyes lit up.

Reigniting: Ten thousand yuan? That generous?
